matrices.answers: (a) SLIDER RANGE SOURCE: the manual Move slider/number/chip get their range from parts.json — `part.config.rotationRangeDeg` (views/setup/calibration.ejs:2910: svMaxDeg = rotationRangeDeg>0 ? that : 180). Everything else — API angle validation, override clamp ceiling, bounds display units, position-display division, preset p normalization — uses the PROFILE's `capability.maxAngleDeg` via maxAngleOf() (server/calibration/router.js:82-87, 709-711, 729; calibration.ejs:1144-1145,1308; routes/setup/calibration.js:199-202). CAN THEY DISAGREE: yes. The router reconciles maxAngleDeg from rotationRangeDeg only on autoGenerated (placeholder) profiles (router.js:201-217, deliberate per d52df26 so measured windows are never silently re-scoped). On a MEASURED profile, changing rotationRangeDeg in parts.json leaves the profile scale untouched: the page then renders a 0-900 slider and a 'multi-turn REAL travel' chip while goto 400s every angle above the profile's 180 (or the reverse: a 0-180 slider on a profile licensed to 900). Failure direction is refusal, not wrong motion, but nothing on the page names the conflict. (b) CONTINUOUS ANGLE SLIDER: No. renderControls gates on parts.json servoType: 'continuous' gets CW/Stop/CCW + speed/duration only (calibration.ejs:2836-2843); the unified page has no angle slider for any type (jog pad only). Even in a kind-mismatch, an {angle} goto against a continuous-servo profile is refused 400 (router.js:707,738-740) — an angle command cannot silently become a timed spin THROUGH THE CALIBRATION API. The one leak is the unified page's PCA-channel 'Test' button, which posts /api/parts/:id/test {action:'moveToAngle', angleDeg:90} to whatever servo is on the channel; hardwareService's continuous fallback converts that to a CW spin at 90% speed for 1000ms (unified-calibration.ejs:1115-1122; services/hardwareService/index.js:675-682) — defect 5. (c) LINEAR ACTUATOR: Yes — position slider 0-1 + Go (goto p, clamped to measured bounds), Extend/Retract jog via jog-raw (unclamped, calibrationOverride + characterId server-side, 30s cap, surfaces safety refusals), Stop, Home-to-endstop with tracker confidence badge, and Set Min/Set Max as physical-endstop declarations that reset the tracker (calibration.ejs:2995-3120; router.js:588-652,744-761,855-911). The only broken piece is Learn Movement (defect 2). (d) KIND DISAGREEMENT: see last matrix row — manual controls follow parts.json, calibration panel and API dispatch follow profile.capability.kind; placeholders self-heal on every profile GET, measured profiles never do (by design), leaving a split-brain page whose angle Move always 400s or whose CW/CCW buttons become 0.1-degree micro-moves; no warning is rendered. NUDGE STEP SIZES (for the map): absolute servo 2/5/15 deg x (maxAngleDeg/180) => 10/25/75 real degrees at 900 (AbsoluteServoAdapter.js:4,95-96); open-loop linear 0.01/0.05/0.15 p (OpenLoopLinearAdapter.js:3); continuous timed spins 200/500/1000 ms at defaultSpeedPct (ContinuousServoAdapter.js:66-68). NOTE: the main page has NO nudge buttons — jogPart() is defined and window-exported but nothing calls it (calibration.ejs:1242,1298; repo-wide grep confirms zero callers), so the deadband-proof multi-turn nudge steps are reachable only from the legacy unified page (which nothing links to) or raw API. MOVE DEFAULT confirmed: slider initializes to mid-travel (450 on the 900-degree head) and Move always sends calibrationOverride:true (calibration.ejs:2911-2913,2942,2949), which skips the calibrated-bounds clamp (router.js:723-729); it does not track current position until after the first move (2959-2960).

matrices.answers: (a) Multi-turn full range: NO. The editor hardcodes a 0-180 slider for every part.type 'servo' (public/js/poses-editor.js:213); the measured window from /poses/api/part-safety can only narrow WITHIN 0-180 (lines 226-227: min raised if lo>0, max lowered only if hi<180). A calibrated 0-900 window on Dragomir part 1 still renders max=180, and a window with lo>180 renders an inverted slider. rotationRangeDeg/capability.maxAngleDeg are never read client-side and are absent from the part-safety payload (services/poses/poseHealth.js:251-266). Bounds ARE sourced correctly server-side — getEffectiveWindow uses store.get(partId, characterId) whose shapeForRead withholds placeholder and degenerate windows (services/poses/poseBounds.js:69-103; server/calibration/store.js:157-172, 206-208). Uncalibrated part: NOT refused or excluded — include stays enabled with only a caution note (poses-editor.js:196-198); health grades it 'degraded' not 'blocked' (poseHealth.js:177-185); execution passes unclamped through applySafetyLimits when the window is null (safetyLimits.js:246-258); only jitter refuses (poseBounds.js:144-151). (b) Continuous servo: NO — no servoType branch exists; it gets the angle slider (poses-editor.js:212) and never CW/stop/CCW+speed/duration. The saved angleDeg executes as a positional command: batchMoveServos excludes multi-turn but not continuous, so the daemon holds a positional pulse = indefinite rotation (services/hardwareService/index.js:2130-2166); the moveToAngle fallback silently converts angle to a 1s timed spin (index.js:675-681). The executor CAN play target.continuous (poseEngine.js:210-218) but the editor cannot author it. (c) Linear actuator: renders extend/retract + speed% + duration ms only (poses-editor.js:248-259); NO position 0-1 control. Test route enforces minP/maxP projection (partsApi.js:311-355) but pose EXECUTION does not (poseEngine.js:222-238 -> controlPart('jog'); safetyLimits.js has no positional actuator handling). (d) Execution path: POST /poses/:id/execute (routes/poses/index.js:73-74) -> posesController.executePose (controllers/posesController.js:173-228; MB_TEST_MODE simulates at 183-190) -> poseEngine.executePose (services/poses/poseEngine.js:20). Per-type bounds re-checks: jitter clamped into the effective window (poseBounds via character-scoped store.get); servo batch re-applies applySafetyLimits per part (index.js:2104-2119) plus a daemon min/max backstop (2151-2163); multi-turn diverted to controlPart (2130-2136) which re-applies safety (1883-1906) and does the single real-degree conversion (694-698 wrapper, 747-754 daemon pulse); eased transitions clamp every frame (transitionEngine.js:388-393, 500-505, each frame -> batchMoveServos with characterId at 515). Actuator/motor/light parts go through executePosePart -> controlPart with characterId (poseEngine.js:193-197) but only duration-cap/retract-block/quarantine apply — no positional bounds. (e) String/Number: no breaking mismatch found. Editor saves numeric partId (parseInt, poses-editor.js:353); poseRepository.validatePose enforces number (poseRepository.js:220-223); every join normalizes via String(): batchMoveServos String(p.id)===String(cmd.partId) (index.js:2091), executePosePart controlPart(String(partId)) (poseEngine.js:204/212/233/243/261), poseHealth String compare (poseHealth.js:102), part-safety map keyed String(partId) on both ends (poseHealth.js:251, poses-editor.js:50-51), editor reload String(pp.partId) for DOM ids (poses-editor.js:570), transitionEngine believed-angle keys template-interpolate identically for 2 vs \"2\" (transitionEngine.js:114-116). Latent: PUT /api/parts/:id rewrites part.id to the string req.params.id (partsApi.js:468) — harmless today because all consumers String()-compare. One CLAUDE.md staleness note: 'GET /api/parts returns raw array' is outdated — it returns {success, parts} (partsApi.js:90), which is what the editor expects.

(line 821) — a timed spin — on a standard or multi-turn pan servo; (2) a part whose config LACKS servoType but whose modelId names a continuous model inherits servoType:'continuous' from data/models/servo_models.json defaults (merge order modelDefaults<config<params, index.js:1860-1865) — an angle command then becomes the 1s spin; (3) params override config in the same merge, so any caller passing params.servoType flips the route (no in-repo runtime path does; /api/parts/:id/test builds servo params fresh, routes/api/partsApi.js:278). The INVERSE gap is worse: batchMoveServos excludes multi-turn from the batch (index.js:2130-2137) but NOT continuous — a pose part carrying angleDeg on a config.servoType:'continuous' PCA part rides the daemon set_angles path (index.js:2138-2165, servo_daemon.py:291-311) as a raw position pulse, which on a continuous servo is a SPEED: it spins indefinitely, no duration, no stop (defect below).

(b) PLACEHOLDER/DEGENERATE REFUSAL — NOT uniform. The store withholds placeholder and degenerate bounds from every get() (server/calibration/store.js:157-172, isDegenerateWindow 85-102, calibratedBounds 110-114), and isDegenerateWindow is enforced at writers, but downstream behavior splits into REFUSE vs DRIVE-UNCLAMPED: REFUSES: head tracking — no usable window means no drive and the claim is released (motionTrackingController.js:587-601 refusal + span>=1 check at 588; scan path 752-757; positional path 846-852; claim release 694-704); head-animation Test Sweep route (routes/setup/head-animation.js:470-477, 409 refused); jaw testJawMovement (services/jawAnimationSuperPowerService.js:893-895) and moveJawToAngle (1162-1165); idle micro-motion skips windowless parts (services/movement/idleLoopService.js:226-227); pose jitter refuses to add variation without a window (services/poses/poseBounds.js:22-27, 143-151). matrices.answers:
(a) OVERRIDES API — POST /setup/calibration/api/parts/:id/overrides, handler at routes/setup/calibration.js:743-768. It accepts ANY key with ANY value: the only validation is that req.body.overrides is an object (747-748). Semantics: value null DELETES the key from part.config; any other value is written verbatim (756-759); result persisted to the node-local per-character parts.json via saveCharacterParts (762). So yes, it can change channel, servoType, rotationRangeDeg, address, audioDeviceId, or invent keys — with zero enum/range/type checking ("channel":"banana" persists). This is the sanctioned bench path: scripts/bench/knight-finish.sh:30-32 and docs/hardware/BENCH-CHECKLIST.md:138 both set servoType/rotationRangeDeg/channel through it. It CANNOT change a part's TYPE: it writes only into part.config; an overrides {"type":"linear_actuator"} lands as config.type, which no code reads (grep of services/routes/server/controllers: zero readers of config.type). Supported non-git paths to convert part 3 servo→linear actuator on the node: (1) PUT /setup/calibration/api/parts/:id (routes/setup/calibration.js:615-677) — spreads updates over the part including `type` (654-660); note config is deep-MERGED there, so stale servo keys (servoType, channel) survive the retype; (2) PUT /api/parts/:id (routes/api/partsApi.js:444-477) — same spread at 468, config replaced only if body carries config. The UI offers no affordance: the Edit form's type field is readonly (views/setup/calibration.ejs:587); the UI-only route is delete part + re-add (POST /setup/calibration/api/parts, routes/setup/calibration.js:552-590). CRITICAL COMPANIONS to a retype: use "linear_actuator" (underscore) — the schema also allows "linear-actuator" (config/schemas/parts.schema.json:19-20) but every calibration-machinery check is exact-match underscore (server/calibration/router.js:228; routes/setup/calibration.js:384,504,1053,1116,1179), so the hyphen form gets no profile and 404s; and manually DELETE the old calibration profile (DELETE /api/calibration/3/profile, server/calibration/router.js:1031-1054) because no retype path rebuilds it (see defects).

(b) RETYPE vs PROFILE (515e782, now server/calibration/router.js:137-170 in getOrAutoCreateProfile): rebuild fires ONLY when profile.autoGenerated is truthy AND the existing capability.kind is continuous-servo or absolute-servo AND part.type === 'servo' (144-149). Placeholder profiles flip standard/multi-turn↔continuous in both directions, re-stamping maxAngleDeg from config.rotationRangeDeg (154-163), flushing the adapter cache and persisting (165-166). A MEASURED profile (autoGenerated false) whose kind now disagrees with parts.json is left completely alone AND THE OPERATOR IS NEVER WARNED — there is no console.warn, no response field, no UI banner for the mismatch case; the only log line (153) fires on the placeholder rebuild. The commit message's "MEASURED profiles are never silently re-typed" is true, but they ARE silently left disagreeing: the calibration surface keeps driving the OLD kind while parts.json declares the new one, indefinitely. Additional subtlety: un-stamping Calibrated (POST /:partId/calibrated false) sets autoGenerated=true (router.js:436) while promising "the captured numbers stay in the file" (384-386) — that flag flip re-arms both the retype rebuild (which overwrites bounds to full-span, 158) and the range reconcile (which overwrites bounds to {0,declared}, 212), so a later kind/range drift will destroy the retired measurement. Cross-family retypes (servo↔linear_actuator) are NOT covered at all — see defects.

(c) capability.maxAngleDeg stamping per profile-build site: YES at router auto-create (server/calibration/router.js:242-246, from config.rotationRangeDeg, omitted when 180); YES at retype rebuild (155-157); YES at the placeholder range reconcile (201-217, which also heals stale 0-180 placeholders — but placeholder-only by design). NO at routes/setup/calibration.js blankProfile (68-84): a profile born there carries hardcoded bounds {0,180} and no maxAngleDeg; savePulse (155-168) creates through it without stamping; only savePosition compensates (189-191, stamped only when declaredRange>0 && !=180 && maxAngleDeg==null) and it does not fix the 0-180 bounds. NO at POST /:partId/profile (router.js:313-372): client capability accepted verbatim — only kind is validated (KNOWN_CAPABILITY_KINDS, 311/334). Mitigations: the blankProfile record is autoGenerated, so shapeForRead withholds its bogus 0-180 bounds from movers (server/calibration/store.js:157-172) and the router reconcile heals it on the next /api/calibration touch; scene-executor preset replay prefers stored angle over p (services/scenes/sceneExecutor.js:76) and savePosition writes both. Residual gap: any consumer of capability.maxAngleDeg between a savePulse-born profile and the next router touch computes over 180 (sceneExecutor.js:60-61; hardwareService invert fullSpan index.js:1923-1925 — the latter has a rotationRangeDeg fallback). ALSO: no (re)build site ever reads the MODEL's rotationRangeDeg — config only — see (d).

(d) MODEL ENTRIES ARE PARTIALLY LIVE, NOT DEAD. Entries verified: servo_gobilda_stingray2 defaults {minPulse 500, maxPulse 2500, neutralPulse 1500, rotationRangeDeg 900, servoType "multi-turn"} (data/models/servo_models.json:105-128); servo_miuzei_mg90s {…, rotationRangeDeg 180, servoType "standard"} (23-43); servo_miuzei_25kg {…, 180, "standard"} (63-82); plus a distinct servo_miuzei_25kg_continuous (83-103). READ paths: controlPart merges model defaults UNDER part.config and params for EVERY hardware command — `Object.assign({}, modelDefaults, normalized, params)` (services/hardwareService/index.js:1859-1865, resolver getModelDefaultsForPart at 105-159, honoring data/character-N/models/ overrides first, 128-134). Therefore defaults.servoType and defaults.rotationRangeDeg DO steer moveToAngle dispatch (index.js:663-704) whenever part.config lacks them — Dragomir part 1's model is an active safety net if config.servoType is ever lost. minPulse/maxPulse/neutralPulse ARE dead on the PCA path: the standard route sends channel+angle only (698-702, daemon 721-737), the multi-turn daemon pulse is hardcoded 500+(real/range)*2000 (748-754), and pca9685.js's pulse-accepting export was removed (services/hardwareService/pca9685.js:100). The display-only reader is GET /setup/calibration/api/parts/:id/effective (routes/setup/calibration.js:842-860). THE ASYMMETRY IS THE HAZARD: the calibration-profile machinery reads config.servoType/config.rotationRangeDeg exclusively (router.js:150,155,205,242; routes/setup/calibration.js:182,939) and never model defaults, so a part relying on its model for type/range drives multi-turn at dispatch while the profile machinery builds a 180-span absolute profile. Also both model-editor UIs cannot represent "multi-turn" (views/setup/models.ejs:269 and views/setup/calibration.ejs:2055 offer only standard|continuous|feedback), and the legacy seeder never emits it (controllers/modelsController.js:71).

(e) NON-CANONICAL servoType STRINGS — the layers disagree on normalization. Dispatch (services/hardwareService/index.js:666-669) lowercases and aliases cont|cr→continuous, positional|position|multi|multi_turn|multi-turn→feedback; ANY other string ('multiturn', ' multi-turn' with whitespace, 'standrad') silently falls into the STANDARD 0-180 path (gate at 721). Calibration router does NOT lowercase: `st === 'continuous'` exact at router.js:150-151 and 233-234, so 'Continuous' builds/rebuilds an absolute-servo profile for a part the dispatch layer will spin. Batch path is robust (lowercased + rotationRangeDeg>0 fallback, index.js:2130-2132). Setup-page status lowercases (routes/setup/calibration.js:492,1298) but the calibration page's own client JS does not (views/setup/calibration.ejs:2795,2864,3938), nor does public/js/manual-controls.js:479, nor detectServoType's config fallback (controllers/motionTrackingController.js:629, which also memoizes servoType until restart, 794-796). No writer validates the string: the overrides API accepts anything, and parts.schema.json declares config as a bare object (config/schemas/parts.schema.json:32), so `npm run validate:schemas` passes any typo. Worst concrete combination is defect #1 below.

matrices.answers: HOW VIEW/CLIENT-JS UNIT TESTS WORK IN THIS REPO: There is no jsdom, happy-dom, or cheerio anywhere (grep of package.json + tests/ = zero hits). Three established patterns: (1) PAGE-SOURCE CONTRACT TESTS (unit tier): mocha + supertest GET the rendered EJS page from a RUNNING server at BASE_URL, slice the inline <script> source between named function markers, and regex-assert on the source text — canonical examples tests/unit/sweep-pacing-main-page.test.js:25-74 (slices 'function sweepLegWaitMs'..'window.runSweepTest', asserts the multi-turn >360 rate branch and sweepLegWaitMs(...currentPartMaxAngleDeg) call sites) and tests/unit/calibrated-stamp-main-page.test.js:32-36 (asserts 'calibratedToggle'/'toggleCalibratedStamp' appear in /setup/calibration HTML). This IS the established pattern for testing EJS-rendered control markup: string/regex assertions against the served page, not DOM execution. Note sweep-pacing defaults BASE_URL to :3000 (line 18) but `npm run test:unit` pins BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 (package.json:17). (2) SOURCE-GREP TESTS: read a service file from disk and regex-assert invariants (tests/unit/pose-engine-targets.test.js:22-49 — every controlPart call passes character context; batchMoveServos gets { characterId }; tests/unit/scene-step-resilience.test.js same style). (3) PLAYWRIGHT for real DOM (tests/browser/*.spec.js); calibration-panels.spec.js:34-53,138-152 only checks the calibration panel shows for a servo and hides for a webcam — nothing per servoType. IN-PROCESS API TEST CONVENTION (the file any new per-type regression should follow): tests/unit/multi-turn-servo.test.js:49-110 — set MB_TEST_MODE=1 + CI=true so services/hardwareService/exec.js simulates and ECHOES wrapper args (observable via result.rawOutput JSON), append synthetic high-ID parts (987xxx) to the selected character's parts.json, mount server/calibration/router.js on a bare express app, snapshot/restore parts.json + data/calibration_profiles.json + data/actuator-positions.json byte-exact in before/after. NPM SCRIPTS PER SUITE: tests/unit (incl. multi-turn-servo, continuous-jog-saturation, sweep-pacing, calibrated-stamp, hardware-safety-limits, invert-single-formula, degenerate-calibration-window) → `npm run test:unit` (== test:smoke, runs in the gate); `npm run test:unit:calibration` runs ONLY calibration-unified-api + webcam-calibration-api (package.json:18) — it does NOT run the multi-turn or continuous-jog suites. tests/system/head-animation.test.js → `npm run test:system:head`; parts-api/hardware → `test:system:parts`; models → `test:system:models`; movement → `test:system:movement`; all → `npm run test:system`. tests/browser → `npm run test:browser` per area `test:browser:calibration|setup|models` — but per CLAUDE.md the working on-node invocation is `MB_USE_RUNNING_SERVER=1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 npx playwright test tests/browser --reporter=list`. tests/hardware (continuous-servo-calibration, linear-actuator-calibration) → `npm run test:hardware` / `test:hardware:servo` / `test:hardware:actuator` — NOT run by `npm test`, `npm run verify`, or the gate (scripts/gate.mjs:47-48 runs only validate:schemas, audit:resolver, audit:independence, test:smoke, test:pact). tests/pact → `npm run test:pact` (in gate). Cross-suite: `node scripts/test-runner.mjs --area ... --suite ...`. WHERE NEW REGRESSION TESTS FOR EACH GAP BELONG: (a) range-scaled 10/25/75 nudge + controlPart end-to-end multi-turn + daemon pulse path → extend tests/unit/multi-turn-servo.test.js (it already owns the 900° synthetic part, simulated-exec echo, and file snapshot conventions); (b) continuous angle-command dispatch behavior → new tests/unit/servo-type-dispatch.test.js (or extend multi-turn-servo.test.js) calling HARDWARE_CONTROLLERS.servo.moveToAngle / controlPart with servoType:'continuous' and asserting the echoed wrapper args are NOT rotate_continuous_pca unless intended; (c) per-type control MARKUP (continuous = CW/stop/CCW and no #ang slider; multi-turn = slider max from rotationRangeDeg incl. the 'multi-turn: 0–900° REAL travel' chip; linear_actuator = laPosSlider 0-1 + extendBtn/stopBtn/retractBtn; servoType select options) → new tests/unit/part-controls-main-page.test.js following sweep-pacing-main-page.test.js exactly (fetch /setup/calibration, slice the renderer source, regex-assert); (d) multi-turn in availableServos whitelist → fix in place at tests/system/head-animation.test.js:339; (e) invert on a declared multi-turn span → extend tests/unit/invert-single-formula.test.js with a capability.maxAngleDeg:900 case; (f) linear-actuator refusals in the default gate → port the validation-only cases (they never energize hardware — that file binds the store to a throwaway file, see tests/hardware/linear-actuator-calibration.test.js:97-190 header) into tests/unit with a synthetic linear part, because calibration-unified-api.test.js:50-51 silently skips all linear rows on any character (like Sir Dragomir, data/character-4/parts.json has NO linear_actuator) that lacks one.

Known/by-design as the operator's measuring tool, but the default target is an invented position: one accidental click commands up to 450 real degrees of travel on the multi-turn neck from wherever it stands — the exact incident class named in the code's own comments (router.js:78-81). CLAUDE.md bars agents from driving this part; the UI default aims an operator's first click at it.
confirmed.failureScenario: Operator selects Head Servo to check its bounds, clicks Move without touching the slider (or fat-fingers Enter in the number box): the head is commanded to real 450 with no bounds clamp; if it was parked near 900 that is ~450 degrees of travel through the cabling in one hop.
confirmed.suggestedFix: On part select, seed the slider/number from GET /:id/position when currentAngle is known and disable Move (with a 'position unknown - jog or home first' hint) when it is not, instead of defaulting to mid-travel.
confirmed.surface: Calibration page (/setup/calibration -> views/setup/calibration.ejs, routes/setup/calibration.js) + legacy unified page (/setup/calibration/unified -> views/setup/unified-calibration.ejs) + calibration API (server/calibration/router.js mounted at /api/calibration, server.js:504; page routes mounted at /setup/calibration, server.js:509). Adapters: server/calibration/adapters/{AbsoluteServoAdapter,ContinuousServoAdapter,OpenLoopLinearAdapter}.js; bounds/trust via server/calibration/store.js (calibratedBounds/isCalibrated/isDegenerateWindow). Grounded against Sir Dragomir (char 4) parts: id 1 Head Servo servoType="multi-turn" rotationRangeDeg=900 ch4, id 2 Jaw Servo standard ch1, id 3 Magic Box Servo standard ch3 (data/character-4/parts.json).

verdict.reasoning: Every cited line verifies: views/setup/calibration.ejs:2938-2942 seeds the angle slider/number to round(svMaxDeg/2)=450 for the 900-degree char-4 Head Servo (data/character-4/parts.json:9,14); Move always posts calibrationOverride:true (2970,2977); server/calibration/router.js:723-729 then clamps only to 0..maxDeg (calibrated bounds skipped); checkSafety (713-714) cannot refuse because config/hardware-safety.json is empty per the 2026-08-20 ruling; controls sync to reality only after a successful Move (2987-2988). The strongest, un-refutable form of the defect is the position-KNOWN case: the page already fetches GET /:id/position on part select (calibration.ejs:1115-1121) and displays the tracked angle in calPositionDisplay, yet renderControls (called at 1068) never receives it — so mid-session the badge can read 900° while the slider beside it reads 450, and re-selecting a part resets controls to the invented mid; one Move click then commands ~450 real degrees through the head cabling, the incident class router.js:78-81 names. This is not barred-by-ruling territory: seeding a UI default from known position is not a safety refusal. Severity is should-fix, not must-fix: the correct control type renders, the correct path is driven, motion happens only on an explicit operator click on the operator's own measuring page, and in the most common state (after service restart, positionState is an in-memory Map, router.js:18, never persisted for absolute servos) currentAngle is null so no seeding is possible and mid-travel is actually the minimax blind default (450 max surprise vs 900 from an endpoint default). Two corrections to the claim: (1) the 'fat-fingers Enter' sub-scenario is invalid — the controls are not inside a form, so Enter in the number box does not trigger Move; (2) the suggested fix's 'disable Move when position unknown' is wrong — nudge already 409s with 'move to an absolute angle (goto) first' (router.js:499-501) and absolute servos have no home (home UI is open-loop-only, calibration.ejs:1154-1157), so disabling goto would make an unknown-position servo immovable from this page, and it adds a motion refusal the 2026-08-20 operator ruling bars.
verdict.correctedFix: In calibration.ejs, pass the /position result into the angle controls instead of only the badge: after loadUnifiedCalibration's position fetch (lines 1115-1121) succeeds with a finite currentAngle for an absolute servo, set #ang/#angNum to Math.round(currentAngle) (note ordering: renderControls(selected) at line 1068 runs before the position fetch resolves, so the seeding must happen in that fetch's callback, and also after nudge/preset/home actions that change position). When currentAngle is null (unknown, e.g. after service restart), do NOT disable Move — goto is the server's documented recovery from unknown position (router.js:499-501) and disabling it would strand absolute servos and re-add a refusal barred by the 2026-08-20 ruling; instead either keep the mid-travel value with a visible 'position unknown — this target is a guess' hint, or render the number input blank so the existing isNaN guard at line 2954-2955 makes Move inert until the operator explicitly chooses a target.

confirmed.title: Multi-turn servo renders a 0-180 slider — full real range never reachable, and a high window inverts the control
confirmed.description: renderPartControls hardcodes min=0/max=180 for every part.type==='servo' and the safety-window overlay (lines 226-227) can only NARROW inside that: min rises if window.lo>0, max drops only if window.hi<180. config.rotationRangeDeg (900 on Dragomir part 1) and capability.maxAngleDeg are never consulted client-side, and /poses/api/part-safety does not carry servoType/range (services/poses/poseHealth.js:251-266). This contradicts commit e99841f's 'UI 0-900' contract for this surface.
confirmed.failureScenario: Dragomir head (part 1, 900°) calibrated with a measured 0-900 window: slider renders 0-180, operator can only author the bottom 20% of travel while the safety note beside it prints 'Safe window 0°-900°' (lines 192-194). Worse: a measured window of e.g. 300-600 yields min=300, max=180 — an invalid inverted range input — and val recomputed to 240; whatever the browser coerces gets saved as angleDeg and played.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In renderPartControls, when the part is multi-turn (part.config.servoType in the multi set or Number(part.config.rotationRangeDeg)>0), base the slider on 0..rotationRangeDeg, then intersect with the part-safety window in real degrees (raise min to lo, lower max to hi, both directions). Also add servoType/rotationRangeDeg to getPartSafetySummary so the client need not rely on /api/parts config shape.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED with file:line evidence. public/js/poses-editor.js:213 hardcodes min=0/max=180 for every part.type==='servo'; config.servoType/rotationRangeDeg are never read anywhere in the file. Dragomir part 1 (data/character-4/parts.json) is multi-turn/900 with NO markers, so the marker branch (lines 215-221) cannot widen the slider. The safety overlay (lines 226-227) is one-directional: min only rises, max only falls below 180 — a measured real-degree window (which is what getEffectiveWindow at services/poses/poseBounds.js:87-89 returns for a calibrated multi-turn post-e99841f; hardware-safety.json is empty so only profile bounds contribute) of 0-900 leaves the slider 0-180 while renderPartSafetyNote (lines 192-194) prints 'Safe window 0°-900°' beside it; a window of 300-600 yields min=300/max=180. getPartSafetySummary (services/poses/poseHealth.js:251-266) indeed omits servoType/range. git show e99841f confirms its 'UI 0-900' work touched only views/setup/calibration.ejs — this surface was missed. views/poses/editor.ejs:163 confirms the script is live. Refutations failed: no markers on part 1 (baseline; markers are a legacy mechanism per routes/setup/jaw-animation.js:499), the 2026-08-20 operator ruling removed safety CAPS not control-range correctness, and no server-side re-scope exists on save (collectPoseParts line 357 saves slider.value verbatim as target.angleDeg; play path treats it as real degrees per e99841f/d52df26). Two corrections to the claim: (1) the inverted-range case is inert, not hazardous — WHATWG range sanitization sets max=min when max<min, so the slider is stuck at lo (e.g. 300), which is inside the measured window; no out-of-window command can be produced by this bug. (2) An unclaimed aggravator: loadPoseIntoEditor (lines 585-590) assigns an existing pose's real-degree angle (e.g. 450) to the 0-180 slider, the browser coerces it to 180, and re-saving silently rewrites the pose — editing any head pose authored via another surface corrupts it. Severity must-fix under this audit's contract: a documented core authoring surface renders the WRONG control for the multi-turn type (80% of head travel unreachable, contradictory safety note, possible inert control, silent data rewrite on edit-resave).
verdict.correctedFix: In renderPartControls (public/js/poses-editor.js:210-235): detect multi-turn from the part data the page already has — /api/parts serves raw parts.json entries including config (routes/api/partsApi.js:82-95) — i.e. part.config && (part.config.servoType === 'multi-turn' || (Number(part.config.rotationRangeDeg) > 0 && Number(part.config.rotationRangeDeg) !== 180)). For such parts base the slider on 0..rotationRangeDeg instead of 0..180 (markers, when present, still override as real degrees). Then intersect with the part-safety window bidirectionally: min = Math.max(min, sSafety.minAngle ?? min); max = Math.min(max, sSafety.maxAngle ?? max); and guard the degenerate result (if min > max, render the card with the control disabled and the window text, never an inverted range input) — the current one-directional conditions at lines 226-227 are what produce the inversion and must be replaced, not just widened. Also clamp/handle loadPoseIntoEditor (lines 585-590): if the stored angleDeg exceeds the rendered slider max, do not let browser coercion silently rewrite it on save — either widen the slider or flag the part. Adding servoType/rotationRangeDeg to getPartSafetySummary (services/poses/poseHealth.js:251-266) is sensible hardening so window semantics are self-describing, but it is optional, not required as the reviewer implied — the client already receives config via /api/parts. Match the existing ES5/IIFE style (var, no arrow functions) per CLAUDE.md.

refuted.title: Overrides tab silently deletes servoType 'multi-turn' — head servo then drives on the 0-180 standard scale
refuted.reasoning: The deletion mechanics are all real: OVERRIDE_SCHEMAS.servo lacks 'multi-turn' (views/setup/calibration.ejs:2055), the select falls to the blank first option on no exact match (2132-2135), collectOverrideFields maps '' to null (2145-2157), and the server deletes null keys (routes/setup/calibration.js:756-758). Save Overrides therefore does strip servoType:'multi-turn' from part.config. But the claimed consequence — moveToAngle routing the head as 'standard' and slamming to real 900° — cannot occur, because the claim misses the model-defaults merge in controlPart: actionParams = Object.assign({}, modelDefaults, normalized(config), params) at services/hardwareService/index.js:1859-1865. The head servo's top-level modelId 'servo_gobilda_stingray2' (data/character-4/parts.json:18) is untouched by the overrides endpoint (it only mutates part.config), and that model's registry entry in data/models/servo_models.json declares defaults {servoType:'multi-turn', rotationRangeDeg:900}. getModelDefaultsForPart (index.js:105-158) resolves it, so after the deletion the drive path still receives servoType 'multi-turn' → normType 'feedback' → the multi-turn branch with the correct real-degree conversion (index.js:666-669, 683-699, 747-770). No goto caller shadows it with an explicit servoType param (AbsoluteServoAdapter.js:118-123 passes only angleDeg+duration; routes/setup/head-animation.js:492 and routes/conversation.js:322 pass only angleDeg). The batch path is independently protected because isMultiTurn also triggers on Number(partCfg.rotationRangeDeg) > 0 (index.js:2130-2132), and rotationRangeDeg:900 is a NON-schema key the Save handler explicitly preserves (calibration.ejs:2213-2219). The UI still renders the 0-900 control (keyed to config.rotationRangeDeg at calibration.ejs:2938, not servoType), and the placeholder-profile kind/range logic is unaffected (server/calibration/router.js:150-158, 201-217 distinguish only continuous-vs-not and read rotationRangeDeg). Semantically, deleting the override is 'release to model default' — the blank option is even rendered '(model: multi-turn)' from d.modelDefaults (calibration.ejs:2129-2133; /effective merge at routes/setup/calibration.js:852-855) — and the effective value is identical before and after, so both Save Overrides and Revert to Model Defaults leave behavior unchanged on this part. Residual fragility (correctness now leans on modelId + the deployed data/models registry; a multi-turn part WITHOUT a modelId would genuinely misroute after this deletion since moveToAngle keys normType on servoType alone) is worth hardening but does not make the claimed scenario real for Sir Dragomir's head, and the operator can express the type via the offered 'feedback' option, which routes identically to multi-turn (index.js:668).

unverified.title: Continuous servo gets an angle slider; the saved angleDeg executes as a held positional pulse (unbounded spin) via the batch path
unverified.description: No servoType branch exists: any type 'servo' part renders the angle slider and saves target:{angleDeg}. At execution poseEngine classifies it into the servo batch (poseEngine.js:102), and batchMoveServos excludes multi-turn (index.js:2130-2136) but NOT continuous — a PCA continuous part lands in pcaPairs and the daemon writes a standard positional pulse (index.js:2138-2199) which a continuous servo interprets as sustained rotation, held until the channel is re-commanded. The non-daemon moveToAngle fallback instead silently converts angle to a 1s timed spin at speed=|angle| (index.js:675-681). Neither is the CW/stop/CCW + speed/duration control the type requires, and the spin has no window to clamp against (continuous profiles carry minP/maxP, not angles).
unverified.failureScenario: Operator re-types a head servo to 'continuous' (or adds one), includes it in a pose at slider value 0: batch daemon writes ~500µs pulse = full-speed rotation held indefinitely; on a neck it wraps cabling exactly like the documented knight incident. The editor UI gave no hint the number was not an angle.
unverified.suggestedFix: Editor: branch on servoType==='continuous' and render CW/stop/CCW + speed + duration, saving target:{continuous:{direction,speedPct,durationMs}} (the executor already handles this shape, poseEngine.js:210-218). Defense in depth: in batchMoveServos, divert servoType 'continuous' parts out of the positional batch the same way multi-turn is diverted, and have servo.moveToAngle refuse (not convert) an angle on a continuous part outside explicit legacy callers.

Mitigated: the record is autoGenerated (shapeForRead withholds the bogus span from movers, store.js:157-172) and the router's reconcile heals it on the next /api/calibration touch (router.js:201-217) — but consumers that read capability.maxAngleDeg directly in the interim compute spans over 180 (services/scenes/sceneExecutor.js:60-61 for presets stored with p only; index.js:1923-1925 invert fullSpan has a config fallback).
unverified.failureScenario: First calibration touch on a fresh multi-turn part is a pulse save on the setup page; before any /api/calibration endpoint runs, a scene replays a p-only preset: fullSpanDeg resolves 180 instead of 900 and the preset lands at a fifth of the intended angle.
unverified.suggestedFix: Stamp maxAngleDeg and bounds from config.rotationRangeDeg inside blankProfile/mutateProfile (the part is loadable there — savePosition already does the lookup).

unverified.title: Un-stamping Calibrated re-arms the placeholder rebuild/reconcile writers, which can overwrite the retired measured bounds — contradicting the endpoint's 'destroys nothing' promise
unverified.description: POST /:partId/calibrated {calibrated:false} sets profile.autoGenerated=true (436) while the endpoint's contract says the captured numbers stay and are merely untrusted (381-386). But autoGenerated=true is exactly the gate for the retype rebuild (144, which REPLACES bounds with full-span at 158) and the range reconcile (201, which REPLACES bounds with {0,declared} at 212). If servoType or rotationRangeDeg has drifted since measurement, the next profile load erases the retired window permanently instead of preserving it for re-blessing.
unverified.failureScenario: Operator un-stamps the head's 120-780 measured window intending to re-verify later; meanwhile a bench override corrects rotationRangeDeg 900->1800 for a rebuilt gearbox; the next GET /profile overwrites bounds to 0-1800 and the hand-measured 120-780 window is gone from the file — the one loss mode the 2026-08-20 .err logging fix was meant to make impossible again, here with no log at all.
unverified.suggestedFix: Track 'placeholder' separately from 'untrusted' (e.g. keep autoGenerated=false and rely on profile.calibrated for trust), or have the rebuild/reconcile writers preserve prior bounds into a retiredBounds field and console.warn to .err when overwriting.

unverified.title: head-animation system test rejects servoType 'multi-turn' — suite fails on Sir Dragomir
unverified.description: The 'should report servo type correctly' assertion whitelists servoType to ['standard','continuous','feedback']. The test resolves CHARACTER_ID from the live selected character, so it encodes a stale type vocabulary as a contract.
unverified.failureScenario: Node has character 4 selected; `npm run test:system:head` (or test:system / npm test) runs; GET /setup/head-animation/api/head-tracking/4 returns availableServos including the multi-turn head; expect(['standard','continuous','feedback']).to.include('multi-turn') throws — a red suite that reads like a head-tracking regression and has nothing to do with one.

unverified.title: Zero coverage: an angle command on servoType 'continuous' silently becomes a 1000 ms timed spin
unverified.description: HARDWARE_CONTROLLERS.servo.moveToAngle converts angleDeg on a continuous-typed part into rotate_continuous_pca cw/ccw at speed=min(100,|angle|) for a hardcoded 1000 ms and returns success (lines 675-682). No test in any tier asserts this dispatch — neither that it happens (pinning intended fallback behavior) nor that a mis-typed non-continuous part is protected from it. The context's correctness property ('an angle command must not silently become a timed spin on a non-continuous part') is entirely unguarded at the seam where it would occur; the existing 515e782 regression test (multi-turn-servo.test.js:216-242) covers only the calibration-profile kind rebuild, not the hardwareService servoType branch that scene steps (sceneExecutor.js:422), pose batches, and /api/parts/:id/test all flow through.
unverified.failureScenario: A stray servoType:'continuous' lands on Sir Dragomir's positional jaw servo (bench click, bad merge of node-local parts.json). Any scene 'servo' step or Pose Editor test command sends moveToAngle angleDeg:90 → the part gets a 90%-speed 1 s open-loop spin, reported success:true. Every current suite stays green.
unverified.suggestedFix: Add a dispatch test (extend tests/unit/multi-turn-servo.test.js or new tests/unit/servo-type-dispatch.test.js, same MB_TEST_MODE+CI simulated-exec echo pattern): call HARDWARE_CONTROLLERS.servo.moveToAngle with servoType:'continuous' and assert the echoed args — deciding first with the operator whether the correct pinned behavior is refusal (preferred: return success:false 'continuous servo takes rotateContinuous, not an angle') or the documented fallback; and assert servoType:'standard'/'multi-turn' never emits rotate_continuous_pca.

unverified.title: Invert on a declared multi-turn span untested
unverified.description: The system-wide invert mirror computes fullSpan from capability.maxAngleDeg (else actionParams.rotationRangeDeg, else 180) so an inverted multi-turn part without measured bounds mirrors across its REAL span (lines 1918-1928). tests/unit/invert-single-formula.test.js covers only measured windows and the legacy 180 fallback (:42-98) — the maxAngleDeg branch has no case. A regression to a hard 180 mirror would turn 'invert' on a 900° part into 180-angle, driving negative/wrong real angles.
unverified.failureScenario: capability.invert is enabled on the knight's 900° head with placeholder bounds 0-900; runtime moveToAngle 700 mirrors as 0+900-700=200 today; a regression to the 180 formula yields 180-700=-520, an out-of-range command whose downstream clamp lands the head at 0 — full travel — with success reported.
unverified.suggestedFix: Add a case to tests/unit/invert-single-formula.test.js with a profile carrying capability.maxAngleDeg:900 and bounds 0-900, asserting the runtime mirror of 700 is 200 (and that the calibration adapter agrees).

unverified.description: The page renders three distinct per-type control sets in client JS (isCont gate at :2864 → CW/stop/CCW deltas, no angle slider; absolute branch :2938-2948 → slider min 0 max svMaxDeg from part.config.rotationRangeDeg with the 'multi-turn: 0–900° REAL travel' chip; linear_actuator :3025-3040 → 0-1 slider + Extend/Stop/Retract), and the part-edit form's servoType select at :2055 offers only ['standard','continuous','feedback'] — 'multi-turn' cannot be selected, so re-typing through this form cannot express the knight's actual type ('feedback' reaches the same dispatch branch via index.js:668 but leaves servoType disagreeing with the vocabulary used by parts.json, the head-animation API, and the isCont/absolute UI gates). The repo has an established page-source test pattern (sweep-pacing-main-page.test.js) but applies it only to sweep pacing and the calibrated stamp; none of the per-type rendering or the select's option list is pinned, so drift like the missing option is invisible to every suite.
